purpose: Contract governance, SDK distribution and cross-repository compatibility. Not a runtime gateway.

authority: Testagram-native access-token issuance and live-session validation
services.auth: Testagram-native short-lived access JWT; PostgreSQL session/account checks on every protected request; opaque rotating refresh token accepted only by /api/auth/refresh; no external identity-provider bearer fallback on end-user routes
services.notes: Current Backend mainline is 4ca5da34222f70b120ec2bb144bc4ec40e6f6218 (merged PR #566 video deletion/staging harness and #567 migration-order guard; prior PR #557 remains in history). It is the sole identity, session, authorization and canonical product-data authority. Creator video channel management, private streaming upload, owner status, explicit publishing and owner-scoped idempotent deletion use authenticated /api/video/* routes to the private Data Centre video worker; the public feed, signed HLS manifest/segments, views, likes and comments also proxy through Backend. Flutter never receives the private service URL. Uploads default private and publishing requires ready processing; HLS playback uses a signed, short-lived token and a bounded streaming proxy that forwards byte-range requests and validates playback-session identifiers. Post-merge mainline checks passed: Backend CI (45891724912), Go security (45891725209), container build (45891725024), self-hosted Compose (45891724908) and workflow syntax (45892003626). InstaBox deployment-input validation passed (45891725014); all production deployment jobs were skipped. The staging video acceptance workflow is manual. Native signup remains fail-closed behind identity review. Messaging, calls and E2EE remain gated; source CI does not establish live provider or production acceptance.

authority: Testagram-native login, refresh, recovery and session restoration
services.auth: Uses Backend-native login and rotating refresh credentials; stores only the refresh token in platform secure storage; access token stays in memory
services.notes: Current Flutter mainline is 07376965588096a689d90c0dc30ca3ed5429f474; Flutter PR #163 CI run 45890527587 passed on the reviewed PR head; post-merge mainline Flutter CI run 45891743771 and container build 45891743596 are running. API contract CI run 45868112697 passed against the current API mainline and pinned client source. PR #163 adds a real Android integration test that loads the exact published staging video into the Flutter feed, waits for native playback and seeks forward. The Backend's manually confirmed staging workflow runs this test before deleting the disposable video. Auth, profile, feed, posts/replies/interactions, threads, discovery/search/hashtags, polls, knowledge, lists, history, notifications, federation preferences, wallet and supported media operations use the public Backend contract. Flutter does not call private microservices directly. Messaging exposes only supported metadata/reaction/delete behavior; plaintext and encrypted send/edit/attachments remain disabled pending E2EE device trust and decryption. Calls and Audio Spaces are lifecycle/UI foundations only pending realtime transport, WebRTC media encryption and an SFU. Monetization destinations are navigable foundations; campaign, earnings, premium/subscription, boost, payout and gifts/tips workflows do not yet have complete Backend ledger/provider contracts. Video service direct ingress remains unavailable and must not be pointed at the general API origin.

services.auth: PLATFORM_INTERNAL_TOKEN for protected platform writes; video and notification user routes validate Backend-native access JWTs against live PostgreSQL session/account state; user tokens are never platform service credentials
services.notes: Current Data Centre mainline is 17d12502019e3837718b02869427248f8267e737 (merged PR #127; prior PR #121 remains in history); PR #127 checks passed and post-merge mainline testagram-vps-ci run 45889734546 passed. Video comments and likes require a native user session and a ready, non-private video. Owner-scoped idempotent DELETE /v1/videos/{video_id} refuses active jobs, cascades video/engagement/job metadata, recomputes channel counts and removes original/HLS/poster media after commit; HLS segments recheck video visibility and readiness on every request. It owns storage mechanics, media lifecycle providers, video processing, notification delivery infrastructure, platform operations and backups; it does not own product identity, visibility or authorization. Backend has typed, direction-specific clients for private media and identity-evidence APIs, with separate service credentials. The generic platform config/events/audit listener is a distinct private control-plane API and is not a product API; no generic Backend client is claimed. The Flutter notification SSE path reads the canonical Backend inbox directly; Data Centre notification workers are not a second inbox authority. The video service listener is not publicly routed by the current Caddy ingress. Live provider, storage durability, staging and restore acceptance remain separate from source CI.

authority: creator video upload and processing lifecycle
video views, likes and comments persistence
owner-scoped video deletion and media cleanup
services.auth: Backend forwards the Testagram-native user access JWT; the video service independently validates the live PostgreSQL user/session and enforces video ownership; no platform service token is substituted for user identity
services.notes: Dedicated Go video service in the Data Centre repository. Backend is the only public ingress and connects through DATA_CENTRE_VIDEO_API_URL; the service listener is private and must not be exposed through Caddy or called directly by Flutter. Uploads begin private, FFmpeg processing must reach ready before publish, signed HLS tokens are checked for every playlist/segment request, and visibility/readiness are rechecked at segment delivery. Views are session-deduplicated; likes are idempotent; comments require native user authentication. PR #127 adds owner-scoped idempotent deletion with active-job protection, transactional metadata/engagement cascade and post-commit original/HLS/poster cleanup. Live upload-to-Android playback/seek and cleanup remain pending the manual staging acceptance workflow.

services.auth: Backend-issued short-lived viewer assertion for private media; separate origin and purge credentials; raw user access JWT is not forwarded as a CDN origin credential
services.notes: Current CDN mainline is e0a6e0fd22c934a5bfb6a0a4b9686f33e0fa5ab7. CI, source verification and container publication passed on that exact SHA. The CDN is a byte-delivery plane for public/private media, HLS/DASH, range requests and cache invalidation; Backend remains the authorization and visibility authority. Private media requires Backend viewer assertions and separately authenticated origins/purge operations. A green build or published image does not prove that media.testagram.site DNS, TLS, edge routing, origin reachability, private-media denial or byte-range behavior are live and correct; those require staging/live endpoint acceptance.

services.auth: Public ActivityPub ingress uses HTTP Signatures; Backend-to-Federation uses a distinct service bearer; Federation-to-Backend uses a different service bearer
services.notes: Current Federation mainline is 0f25d853e5ea5ac546eb1d05847086d387eb2a1c; CI and image publication passed on that exact SHA. Federation owns ActivityPub/AT Protocol protocol state, keys, inbox/outbox and remote delivery; Backend remains authoritative for local identities, follows, blocks, visibility and moderation. The Backend private bridge and protocol adapters are source-present, but delivery/inbox/outbox workers remain disabled by default until signatures, consent, replay protection, idempotency, durability, interoperability and staging gates pass. Source CI is not proof of live federation interoperability.

authority: ranking order and ranking scores only
ranking of Backend-authorized public hashtag candidates
services.notes: Current Algorithm mainline is 3b6a54d5978f8dc33b853698366c0adc110f9614; ranking CI and image publication passed on that exact SHA. Backend sends bounded, already-authorized candidate IDs to private ranking endpoints; Algorithm returns ordering/scores only.
